title: Salvation and Baptism
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Salvation and baptism teaches that baptism publicly identifies believers with Jesus Christ and His people. Baptism does not replace faith in Christ, but visibly declares union with His death, burial, and resurrection.
summary: Salvation and baptism teaches that baptism publicly identifies believers with Jesus Christ and His people. Baptism does not replace faith in Christ, but visibly declares union with His death, burial, and resurrection.
christFocus: Jesus Christ commands baptism and gives it meaning through His saving work. In baptism, believers publicly confess that their hope rests in the crucified and risen Lord.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Baptism is closely connected to discipleship and public identification with Christ. The risen Lord commands His people to make disciples, baptizing them and teaching them to obey all He commanded.

Baptism points to union with Christ in His death and resurrection. It visibly proclaims that the believer’s old life has been judged in Christ and that new life has begun in Him.

Baptism does not save apart from Christ and faith. Its power is not in water as a mechanical act, but in what it signifies: appeal to God, union with Christ, cleansing, and public allegiance to Him.

Baptism also identifies believers with the church. Those who receive the Gospel are not meant to remain hidden or isolated, but to confess Christ before others.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people treat baptism as unnecessary, while others trust the act itself apart from living faith. This doctrine keeps baptism important without making it a substitute Savior.

For new believers, baptism is a clear step of obedience and public testimony. It says, “I belong to Jesus Christ.”

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: If you have trusted Christ, do not treat baptism as optional or meaningless. Receive it as a public act of obedience and identification with Jesus. If you teach others, explain baptism clearly so people look through the sign to the Savior it proclaims.
